newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends flat as nearby spread grows.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends flat as nearby spread grows.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled a quiet session unchanged as trade buying in the spot month drove a wedge in the nearby spread, dealers said.
Spot March closed at a 0.16 cent premium to benchmark May, compared with a 0.01 cent premium after the previous close.

Traders cited short-covering from Far Eastern houses and speculative rolling of March contracts into May. Steady trade and producer scale-up selling beginning at 10.90 cents in May limited gains, they added.
May finished at 10.89 cents, unchanged from the previous settlement. The contract ranged from 10.93 to 10.85 cents during the session. March ended up 0.15 cent to 11.05 cents.
An estimated 16,107 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Wednesday's official volume of 24,168 lots.
Aggressive fund selling is expected to emerge below 10.75 cents, the firm downside target basis the May contract. Lighter support was seen at 10.80 cents in May and resistance at at 11.00 cents.
Open interest in the March contract fell 3,073 lots to 8,138 lots as of the close Wednesday.
Friday is the last trading day for March sugar.
